# Team 4 (PWA & Local Operations) batch — cold review

**Reviewer:** Claude Sonnet 5, orchestrating. Generated by `qwen3.8:27b` via `run_team4_batch.py`
(the same five-fix template validated on Team 1, unchanged), 10 tasks, ~18 minutes wall-clock
(`_batch.log`). This review reads every generated file directly against the real `ts5` source
tree and live `ttod.yml`.
**Date:** 2026-09-11

## Verdict

**Promotable, after real fixes applied in this review.** The path-discipline fix held perfectly
a third time (zero wrong-module citations, despite this module's files being scattered across
`public/`, `src/layouts/`, `src/lib/`, and the repo-root `caddy/` — the most path-fragmented
module forged so far). But two defect classes returned that Team 1's batch had been clean of:
one sibling-scope leak (into Task 5, not the Task 2/3 pair this review specifically flagged as
at-risk beforehand) and a recurrence of Team 2's very first defect — a skill-template
meta-instruction echoed verbatim into output — in two separate tasks. A third, new issue also
showed up: heavy over-concentration on two quotes across the batch.

## What was checked

1. **Path grounding** — every file-path claim checked against the real tree, including the two
   paths flagged in the prompt as easy to mis-nest (`public/ASSIGNMENT.md` under `public/` not
   `src/`; `caddy/Caddyfile` at the repo root, not under `services/frontend`). All 10 sheets cite
   only real paths, correctly rooted. `CACHE_NAME='ttod-pwa-stub-v1'`, `PROOF_ASSET=
   '/visual-system/tokens.css'`, the exact `db.ts` export names, and `OfflineLogEntry` at
   `domain.ts:61` were all independently verified against the real source. Zero drift.
2. **Sibling-scope discipline** — read all 7 full sheets against every other item's title. Items
   2 and 3 (the pair this review's own prompt specifically warned was most likely to blur, being
   two adjacent facets of the same caching system) held the line cleanly — Task 2 explicitly
   scoped itself to "one content target," Task 3 explicitly noted its "static asset set" clause
   overlaps Task 2 and stated the "Network-First API" half is out of its own scope too. The leak
   instead hit **Task 1 → Task 5**: Task 1 ("service-worker lifecycle correctness") restated
   Task 5's entire "Install-quality checks" deliverable (manifest icon sizes, Lighthouse
   installability) as its own §2 worked example, §3 what-has-to-be-done step 2, and §4 success
   criterion 2. **Fixed by hand**: stripped the manifest/Lighthouse content from all three
   sections, added an explicit hand-off note to Task 5, corrected §5's test-shape and oral-defense
   bullets to match.
3. **Meta-instruction echo (Team 2's original defect, recurred)** — Task 2 and Task 6 both
   surfaced a near-verbatim restatement of the assignment-forger skill's own §5 template
   instruction ("Every mention of testing, on every task... links Unit 5... the same way §1 links
   Unit 3... this is currently missing from the published site's own testing rows... close it
   here, don't reproduce the gap") as visible sheet prose — Task 6's copy was closer to verbatim
   than Task 2's paraphrase. This is the exact failure class the `NO_ECHO_RULE` (present in every
   full-sheet prompt since the Team 2 reforge) is meant to prevent, and it held across Team 3's
   and Team 1's batches with zero recurrence — its first reappearance in four batches. **Fixed by
   hand** in both files: removed the instructional wrapper, kept the genuine Unit 5 link inline
   where the content actually needed it.
4. **Quote citation integrity** — every distinct cited id (`wis-009`, `arch-027`, `arch-001`,
   `arch-029`, and the two swapped in during this review, `arch-013` and `wis-007` and `qa-003`)
   checked by script against live `ttod.yml`: all real, all exact text matches, all present in the
   64-quote pwa pool. Zero hallucinations — this discipline has now held clean across all four
   batches without exception.
5. **Quote repetition — the most concentrated of any batch, fixed.** As generated: `arch-027`
   cited 4 times (tasks 2, 3, 5, 6) and `wis-009` cited 3 times (tasks 1, 4, 7) — 7 of the 10
   tasks drew from only two quotes, despite a 64-entry pool and the running already-used list
   being supplied every time. Assessed each use on fit rather than mechanically diversifying:
   `arch-027`'s own `teaches` field literally says "Cache is not a bug—it is a feature
   misunderstood," an unusually exact match for Task 3 (cache policy) and a strong measure-first
   match for Task 6 (performance budget) — both **kept**. Tasks 2 and 5 were weaker fits riding
   the same quote by default. **Fixed by hand**: Task 2 → `wis-007` ("First make it work" — a
   precise match for a task explicitly scoped to one minimal, working proof rather than the
   systematic policy Task 3 owns). Task 5 → `arch-013` ("One source of truth, one place to
   change" — the sheet's own §5 already independently calls the manifest "the single source of
   truth for the app's installability metadata," so this pairing is grounded in the sheet's own
   language, not imposed). Task 7 (`wis-009`, the weakest of its three uses — testing isn't really
   about "updating without shattering") → `qa-003` ("a system without clear layers... technically
   functional, emotionally devastating" — a strong fit for Task 7's own explicit split between
   queue-logic tests and banner-state tests). Final tally: three pairs (`arch-027`, `wis-009`,
   `arch-001`), no repeat above 2×, and every remaining pair independently justified by a specific
   textual match, not just "no worse alternative existed."
6. **Missing `## Closing` heading** — Task 1 went straight from §5 into the quote block with no
   heading, the only sheet across all four batches to omit it entirely (not caught by the
   header-line rule, which governs the *metadata* line, not this heading). **Fixed by hand.**
7. **Orphan scope — worked as designed, for the first time.** The module's own Acceptance
   criterion 4 (a full CI/CD pipeline design — GitHub Actions gate, five-minute budget, no deploy
   job, no secrets) is real, assessed, and absent from both the board and `tasks.md` — the most
   completely undocumented scope item found in any batch so far. Task 1 surfaced it explicitly
   under its own "## Finding: Real, uncounted module scope" heading, exactly as instructed and
   exactly as Team 2's and Team 3's batches failed to do consistently. Left as-is; a genuine
   improvement worth keeping in the driver template's phrasing for Team 5.
8. **Header numbering / `Area(s)` field drift** — Task 10's header reads `Area(s): PWA & Local
   Operations` where the supplied board data said `Process` (also observed, unflagged, in Team 1's
   and Team 3's batches for their own final design-decision tasks). Judged a benign, arguably more
   informative deviation each time — not fixed here either, for consistency with that standing
   judgment call.

## Disposition

Promoted out of `_draft-team4/` into `docs/DEV_PLAN/ASSIGNMENTS/` proper (10 files,
`ASSIGNMENT-pwa-task1.md` through `task10.md`). Not published to `docs/public/` or the `ts5`
worktree — separate, later, explicit step per the forger skill's own rule.

## Carried forward to the skill / next batch (Team 5, the last one)

- The `NO_ECHO_RULE`'s failure on the exact same sentence Team 2 originally leaked suggests that
  specific instruction is unusually prone to being read as content rather than meta-instruction —
  worth rephrasing in the skill's own §5 template guidance itself (not just the driver prompt) so
  it reads less like a sentence that could belong in a sheet's own voice.
- Add one more explicit self-check line for future full-sheet prompts: "an item titled 'X' should
  never contain another item's own title's subject as a completed success criterion — if your
  Task 1 sheet name-checks Task 5's title, that is the leak, regardless of which two items on the
  board it happens to be."
- On quote diversity: consider capping repeats at 2× programmatically (reject and retry a 3rd+
  use of the same id) rather than relying on the "already used" list plus a judgment instruction —
  this batch shows the soft instruction alone is not sufficient at model-discretion boundaries.
